cases.sentence: На ___ у Багратиона в 9 часов дело еще не начиналось.
cases.explain: «правом фланге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: On our right flank commanded by Bagratión, at nine o’clock the battle had not yet begun. Not wishing to agree to Dolgorúkov’s demand to commence the action, and wishing to avert responsibility from himself, Prince Bagratión proposed to Dolgorúkov to send to inquire of the commander in chief. Bagratión knew that as the distance between the two flanks was more than six miles, even if the messenger were not killed (which he very likely would be), and found the commander in chief (which would be very difficult), he would not be able to get back before evening.

cases.sentence: Багратион оглянул свою свиту своими большими, ничего невыражающими, невыспавшимися глазами, и невольно замиравшее от волнения и надежды ___ Ростова первое бросилось ему в глаза.
cases.explain: «детское лицо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Bagratión cast his large, expressionless, sleepy eyes round his suite, and the boyish face of Rostóv, breathless with excitement and hope, was the first to catch his eye. He sent him.

cases.explain: «передней линии» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: He was riding almost along the front line. A handful of men came galloping toward him. They were our Uhlans who with disordered ranks were returning from the attack. Rostóv got out of their way, involuntarily noticed that one of them was bleeding, and galloped on.

cases.sentence: ___, огромный ростом рябой мужчина, злобно нахмурился, увидав перед собой Ростова, с которым он неминуемо должен был столкнуться.
cases.explain: «Крайний кавалергард» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The last of the Horse Guards, a huge pockmarked fellow, frowned angrily on seeing Rostóv before him, with whom he would inevitably collide. This Guardsman would certainly have bowled Rostóv and his Bedouin over (Rostóv felt himself quite tiny and weak compared to these gigantic men and horses) had it not occurred to Rostóv to flourish his whip before the eyes of the Guardsman’s horse. The heavy black horse, sixteen hands high, shied, throwing back its ears; but the pockmarked Guardsman drove his huge spurs in violently, and the horse, flourishing its tail and extending its neck, galloped on yet faster. Hardly had the Horse Guards passed Rostóv before he heard them shout, “Hurrah!” and looking back saw that their foremost ranks were mixed up with some foreign cavalry with red epaulets, probably French. He could see nothing more, for immediately afterwards cannon began firing from somewhere and smoke enveloped everything.

cases.sentence: Вороная, тяжелая, пятивершковая лошадь шарахнулась, приложив уши; но рябой кавалергард всадил ей с размаху в бока ___, и лошадь, взмахнув хвостом и вытянув шею, понеслась еще быстрее.
cases.explain: «огромные шпоры» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Едва кавалергарды миновали Ростова, как он услыхал их крик: «Ура!» и оглянувшись увидал, что передние ряды их смешивались с чужими, вероятно французскими, кавалеристами в ___.
cases.explain: «красных эполетах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: — сказал Борис, улыбаясь тою счастливою улыбкой, которая бывает у ___, в первый раз побывавших в огне.
cases.explain: «молодых людей» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I say, we’ve been in the front line! Our regiment attacked!” said Borís with the happy smile seen on the faces of young men who have been under fire for the first time.

cases.sentence: — кричал Берг, такой же оживленный, как и Борис, подбегая с ___, — граф, я в правую руку ранен (говорил он, показывая кисть руки, окровавленную, обвязанную носовым платком) и остался во фронте.
cases.explain: «другой стороны» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Count! Count!” shouted Berg who ran up from the other side as eager as Borís. “Count! I am wounded in my right hand” (and he showed his bleeding hand with a handkerchief tied round it) “and I remained at the front. I held my sword in my left hand, Count. All our family—the von Bergs—have been knights!”

cases.sentence: Граф, держу шпагу в ___: в нашей породе фон Бергов, граф, все были рыцари.
cases.explain: «левой руке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: Дурное предчувствие, нашедшее вдруг на Ростова, подтверждалось всё более и более, чем дальше он въезжал в занятое толпами ___ пространство, находящееся за деревнею Працом.
cases.explain: «разнородных войск» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The foreboding of evil that had suddenly come over Rostóv was more and more confirmed the farther he rode into the region behind the village of Pratzen, which was full of troops of all kinds.
